text:
alex: heads-up — saw a multi-org 429 spike this morning, but it looks like a handful of keys causing most of the noise. digging in dashboard now. :mag:

maria: can you paste the query? i want to see if it's per-key burst vs sustained quota exhaustion.

alex: using the new per-key heatmap panel on /dashboards/quota-insights — it shows intensity by key and minute. here's the PromQL i'm scribbling:

```
sum by(org_id, api_key) (rate(response_429_total[1m])) / max(1, sum by(org_id, api_key) (rate(req_count_total[1m]))) > 0.05
```

alex: basically trying to find keys that have >5% 429s in a rolling minute.

jen: 5% in a minute seems noisy for large customers. maybe use a windowed approach: 1m for burst detection + 5m sustained indicator.

maria: agreed. split alerts: 
- burst alert (1m, high severity if >X keys cross threshold)
- exhaustion alert (5m sustained high 429 ratio for org)

jen: i can add the 1m burst panel and a separate 5m alarm in grafana. for burst alert, we should require absolute QPS > Y to avoid tiny keys flapping.

alex: +1 on absolute QPS floor. the per-key heatmap also helps CS identify which API keys to call before paging the oncall.

tom: from CS perspective — we need both an automated playbook link in the alert and a lightweight annotation that says whether this is 'billing/ratelimit' vs 'service-failure'. right now alerts just say 429 spike and we waste time.

alex: good call. we can enrich alert payload with labels: {reason: "quota", org_id: .., key_rank: "top3"}. grafana alert supports custom annotations.

jen: thinking about alert noise: during deploy windows we see transient 429s as nodes drain. propose suppressing burst alerts for 10m after any rolling deploy tag on infra.

maria: we already tag deploys in metrics via `deploy_event{service="inference", tag=...}`. can add `unless` clause in PromQL to mute alerts while deploy_event[10m] > 0. but be careful — that could hide true quota problems during a deploy.

alex: what about a reduced-severity alert during deploy windows instead of full suppression? e.g., severity=warning, only page when sustained 5m.

tom: that would help CS triage — warning goes to #cs-ops with playbook link, page only for sustained.

maria: action items I see:
1) jen to add per-key heatmap + two alert rules (burst 1m, sustained 5m) with QPS floor.
2) alex to add alert enrichment labels and dashboard drilldown link.
3) jen + maria to add deploy-aware severity logic (warning vs page).
4) tom to update CS playbook with steps to identify top offending keys and contact template.

jen: i'll PR new panels and rule snippets. sample alert rule I'm going to start from:

```
# burst alert (non-paging)
ALERT PerKey429Burst
IF sum by(api_key, org_id) (rate(response_429_total[1m])) > 0.05
AND sum by(api_key, org_id) (rate(req_count_total[1m])) > 10
FOR 1m
ANNOTATIONS {runbook="https://redwood.internal/playbooks/quota-429"}
LABELS {severity="warning"}
```

jen: and the sustained paging rule:

```
ALERT Org429Sustained
IF sum by(org_id) (sum by(api_key) (rate(response_429_total[5m]))) / sum by(org_id) (sum by(api_key) (rate(req_count_total[5m]))) > 0.03
FOR 5m
LABELS {severity="page", team="oncall"}
```

maria: looks good. let's also add an aggregation that counts distinct keys contributing >10% to org 429s — if count > 3 then escalate faster.

alex: UI request: in Console route page, show "Recent 429 contributors" mini-table with top 10 keys and quick actions (disable key, throttle, contact owner). can we wire that to the same telemetry?

jen: doable. backend just needs an endpoint that returns top keys for org over last N minutes. i'll make it return `[{api_key, 429_pct, qps}]`.

tom: CS wants a 'soft limit' flag that non-paging 429s return a `429-warning` header so clients can surface a nicer UX. is that realistic?

maria: that's productish and not a runtime change we can do quickly — but we can add a `X-Quota-Advisory: true` header for requests that are close to quota. low-effort?

alex: low-effort and helpful. put behind feature flag so only opt-in orgs get it. then CS can test without affecting global clients.

jen: i'll add a feature-flagged response header path in the rate limiter middleware. simple config: `advisory_threshold_pct: 0.85` -> add header when usage > threshold.

maria: one more ops note — update the escalations: if Org429Sustained fires, page oncall and auto-create a Jira with the top 5 keys attached. helps SRE + CS coordinate quickly.

tom: i'll draft the CS playbook steps: check dashboard, copy top keys, confirm billing limits, reach out using template, escalate if org says it's not them. also include the quick query to list keys by 429 ratio.

alex: marking this thread for follow-up. i'll ping once i see jen's PR. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy finished: service=inference tag=release-2026.03.17 commit=abc123 :rocket:

maria: deploy note — remember to watch whether suppression logic accidentally silences sustained alerts during deploy. will validate with synthetic load test after PR merged.

jen: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/grafana/pulls/457 — includes panels, rules, and alert annotations. please review.

alex: reviewing now. tagging @pagerduty-bot to verify routing labels.

pagerduty-bot: incident routing test successful for labels {team="oncall", severity="page"}.

alex: all right — moving to implement console mini-table next week. will follow up with screenshots.

tom: thanks! CS will prep the contact template and runbook updates.

maria: closing loop: after PR lands we'll run a replay of last week's spike in staging to verify signal fidelity and noise reduction.

alex: done — great collaboration.
